title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 English Language and Literature (184) · Crash revision of reading, grammar, writing and literature (2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written from this video's script, its worksheet and the NCERT/CBSE material it cites, modelled on most-repeated / high-weightage question types in CBSE Sample Question Papers and past board papers. Practice for readiness only: not predictions of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number.

patterns.T8: Analytical paragraph: structure and data use

S1.name: Reading Skills
S1.tip: Read the questions first, then the passage, and underline the answer lines. Vocabulary = meaning in that sentence. For charts: title, units, highest, lowest. Answers must point back to the text.
S1.ncert: CBSE English (184) SQP 2026-27 Section A (Q1, Q2); practise one discursive and one case-based passage a day

S2.name: Grammar
S2.tip: Neither…nor: verb agrees with the nearer subject. Each / every / a bunch of → singular verb. few (countable) vs little (uncountable). since / for → present perfect. Yes/no question → asked if / whether + statement order.
S2.ncert: CBSE English (184) SQP 2026-27 Q3 (gap filling, error correction, reported speech); Curriculum 2026-27 grammar list

S3.name: Formal Letter
S3.tip: Format: sender's address → date → receiver (designation first) → subject → salutation → body → close → name. Body: purpose → issue and effects → solutions → thanks. 100–120 words.
S3.ncert: CBSE English (184) SQP 2026-27 Q4 and Marking Scheme (format 1, content 2, organisation 1, accuracy 1)

S4.name: Analytical Paragraph
S4.tip: Intro (what, where, when) → main trend with real numbers and one comparison → conclusion. Never add opinions the data does not support.
S4.ncert: CBSE English (184) SQP 2026-27 Q5 and Marking Scheme (content 2, organisation 2, accuracy 1)

S5.name: First Flight Prose 1
S5.tip: For each text, know one theme word, the main characters and one message: A Letter to God (faith, irony), Mandela (freedom, courage), Two Stories about Flying, Anne Frank (loneliness, wit), Glimpses of India.
S5.ncert: NCERT First Flight: A Letter to God; Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom; Two Stories about Flying; From the Diary of Anne Frank; Glimpses of India

S6.name: First Flight Prose 2
S6.tip: Mijbil (human–animal bond, humour), Madam Rides the Bus (curiosity, first brush with death), Sermon at Benares (death is universal), The Proposal (farce on greed).
S6.ncert: NCERT First Flight: Mijbil the Otter; Madam Rides the Bus; The Sermon at Benares; The Proposal

S7.name: First Flight Poems 1
S7.tip: Link each poem to its symbol: crow and hemlock (Dust of Snow), fire = desire and ice = hatred, cage vs jungle (Tiger), the lost ball (accepting loss).
S7.ncert: NCERT First Flight poems: Dust of Snow; Fire and Ice; A Tiger in the Zoo; How to Tell Wild Animals; The Ball Poem

S8.name: First Flight Poems 2
S8.tip: Amanda (child's need for freedom; repeated name = nagging), The Trees (nature reclaiming freedom), Fog (extended cat metaphor), Custard (don't judge by appearances), Anne Gregory (inner vs outer beauty).
S8.ncert: NCERT First Flight poems: Amanda!; The Trees; Fog; The Tale of Custard the Dragon; For Anne Gregory

S9.name: Footprints Without Feet 1
S9.tip: Triumph of Surgery (pampering harms), Thief's Story (trust and education), Midnight Visitor (wit beats force), Question of Trust (the trickster is tricked), Footprints (science without ethics).
S9.ncert: NCERT Footprints without Feet: A Triumph of Surgery; The Thief's Story; The Midnight Visitor; A Question of Trust; Footprints without Feet

S10.name: Footprints Without Feet 2
S10.tip: Making of a Scientist (curiosity + persistence), The Necklace (vanity and irony), Bholi (education gives dignity), Book that Saved the Earth (arrogance mocked).
S10.ncert: NCERT Footprints without Feet: The Making of a Scientist; The Necklace; Bholi; The Book that Saved the Earth

questions.question: For a question based on a chart or table in a reading passage, what should you check first?
questions.explanation: Title and units tell you what is measured; the highest and lowest values anchor most answers.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Reading Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Only the colours used
Its title, units, and the highest and lowest values
The number of words in the passage
The last line of the passage only

questions.question: Read the passage. “Every Saturday, the families of Lakeview Colony used to dump their unwanted things on one heap. Last year, two students set up a 'swap shelf' in the community hall. People now leave books, toys and utensils they no longer need, and others take them home free. In twelve months, the colony's weekly garbage fell from about 80 kg to 60 kg. Not everyone was convinced at first; some called it 'a shelf of junk'. Today, even those critics drop by on Saturdays.” The writer's attitude towards the swap shelf is:
questions.explanation: The writer reports its success and ends with even the critics coming round: an approving tone.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Reading Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Critical
Indifferent
Appreciative
Mocking

questions.question: Read the passage. “Every Saturday, the families of Lakeview Colony used to dump their unwanted things on one heap. Last year, two students set up a 'swap shelf' in the community hall. People now leave books, toys and utensils they no longer need, and others take them home free. In twelve months, the colony's weekly garbage fell from about 80 kg to 60 kg. Not everyone was convinced at first; some called it 'a shelf of junk'. Today, even those critics drop by on Saturdays.” In this passage, 'convinced' means:
questions.explanation: Meaning in context: people were not yet persuaded that the shelf was useful. 'Found guilty' is a different word (convicted).
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Reading Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Found guilty of a crime
Forced to take part
Persuaded that the idea was good
Confused about the rules

questions.question: Read the passage. “Every Saturday, the families of Lakeview Colony used to dump their unwanted things on one heap. Last year, two students set up a 'swap shelf' in the community hall. People now leave books, toys and utensils they no longer need, and others take them home free. In twelve months, the colony's weekly garbage fell from about 80 kg to 60 kg. Not everyone was convinced at first; some called it 'a shelf of junk'. Today, even those critics drop by on Saturdays.” By what percentage did the colony's weekly garbage fall?
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Reading Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Read the passage. “Every Saturday, the families of Lakeview Colony used to dump their unwanted things on one heap. Last year, two students set up a 'swap shelf' in the community hall. People now leave books, toys and utensils they no longer need, and others take them home free. In twelve months, the colony's weekly garbage fell from about 80 kg to 60 kg. Not everyone was convinced at first; some called it 'a shelf of junk'. Today, even those critics drop by on Saturdays.” What does the last line, 'even those critics drop by on Saturdays', suggest?
questions.explanation: Inference: the people who mocked it now use it, so the shelf has proved its worth.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Reading Skills; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The critics were paid to use the shelf
The idea has won over people who once doubted it
The shelf is now closed on other days
The critics come to complain every week

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the coach nor the players ___ happy with the result.'
questions.explanation: With neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'players' (plural): were.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Grammar; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: was
is
were
has been

questions.question: Choose the correct determiner: 'There is ___ milk left in the jug, so please buy some.'
questions.explanation: Milk cannot be counted, so 'little' (not 'few').
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Grammar; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: few
many
a few
little

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'My cousin ___ in Pune since 2019.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' + a point in time → present perfect: has lived.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Grammar; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: lived
is living
has lived
lives

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: Riya said to me, “Are you coming to the match tomorrow?”
questions.explanation: Yes/no question → asked if/whether; statement order (I was coming); tense back-shift; tomorrow → the next day.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Grammar; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Riya asked me whether was I coming to the match tomorrow.
Riya said to me that I am coming to the match tomorrow.
Riya asked me are you coming to the match tomorrow.
Riya asked me if I was coming to the match the next day.

questions.question: Find the error and its correction: 'The bunch of keys were found under the sofa after a long search.'
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the bunch' (singular), so the verb must be 'was'.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Grammar; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: after → before
were → was
under → below
found → find

questions.question: Which is the correct order for the top of a formal letter?
questions.explanation: Format: sender's address, date, receiver's designation and address, subject, salutation, then body, close and name.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Formal Letter; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Salutation → Sender's address → Date → Subject
Subject → Receiver's address → Date → Sender's address
Date → Salutation → Subject → Sender's address
Sender's address → Date → Receiver's designation and address → Subject → Salutation

questions.question: In the CBSE marking of the 5-mark formal letter, how many marks are given for content?
questions.explanation: Format 1, content 2, organisation 1, accuracy 1 = 5.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Formal Letter; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: You are writing to the editor of a newspaper about broken footpaths near a busy market. Which is the best subject line?
questions.explanation: A good subject line is short and states the exact issue and place.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Formal Letter; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Subject: Letter
Subject: I am very angry
Subject: Hello Sir, please read this
Subject: Urgent need to repair broken footpaths near Green Park market

questions.question: How are the 5 marks of the analytical paragraph divided in the CBSE marking scheme?
questions.explanation: Analytical paragraph: content 2, organisation 2, accuracy 1 (the letter has a format mark instead).
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Analytical Paragraph; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Content 5
Format 1, content 2, organisation 1, accuracy 1
Content 3, accuracy 2
Content 2, organisation 2, accuracy 1

questions.question: A bar graph shows the average daily screen time of students of a school from 2022 to 2025. Which is the best opening line?
questions.explanation: Open with what the data shows, its subject and its time frame, with no opinion.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Analytical Paragraph; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The bar graph shows the average daily screen time of students of a school from 2022 to 2025.
Phones are ruining the lives of students today.
I think students should stop using phones.
Screen time is the biggest problem in the world.

questions.question: The same graph shows 2 hours a day in 2022 and 5 hours a day in 2025. Which sentence uses the data correctly?
questions.explanation: 5 − 2 = 3 hours, and 5 is 2.5 times 2, so 'more than double' is right; 'exactly doubled' is wrong; the marks claim is not in the data.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Analytical Paragraph; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Students' marks fell because of their phones.
Screen time fell by 3 hours a day.
Screen time rose by 3 hours a day, to more than double its 2022 level.
Screen time exactly doubled between 2022 and 2025.

questions.question: In 'A Letter to God', what destroys Lencho's crop?
questions.explanation: A hailstorm ruins the corn and beans, and Lencho writes to God for help.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: First Flight Prose 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: A flood
A forest fire
A swarm of locusts
A hailstorm

questions.question: What is ironic about the end of 'A Letter to God'?
questions.explanation: The people who helped him are the ones he suspects: irony, alongside his unshakeable faith.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: First Flight Prose 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Lencho calls the post-office employees 'a bunch of crooks' though they gave him the money
The rain destroys the post office
Lencho returns the money to God
The postmaster refuses to read the letter

questions.question: In 'Long Walk to Freedom', what are the 'twin obligations' every man has?
questions.explanation: Mandela says every man has obligations to his family and to his people and country.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: First Flight Prose 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: To his job and to his bank
To his family and to his people and country
To his religion and to his property
To his school and to his friends

questions.question: In 'From the Diary of Anne Frank', why does Mr Keesing set Anne extra essays?
questions.explanation: Punished for talking, Anne answers with witty essays ('chatterbox'), and wins Mr Keesing over.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: First Flight Prose 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: She fails her maths test
She is late every day
She forgets her homework
She talks too much in class

questions.question: On her way back from town in 'Madam Rides the Bus', what changes Valli's mood?
questions.explanation: The dead cow is Valli's first brush with death; she comes back quieter.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: First Flight Prose 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Being scolded by the conductor
Seeing a cow that has been killed on the road
Missing the bus home
Losing her coins

questions.question: What does Kisa Gotami learn in 'The Sermon at Benares'?
questions.explanation: She finds no house where no one has died and realises death is universal.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: First Flight Prose 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Only the poor suffer loss
Prayer can bring the dead back
Death is common to all, so grief must be accepted
Mustard seed can cure death

questions.question: In Chekhov's 'The Proposal', Lomov and Natalya quarrel over:
questions.explanation: The proposal is lost in fights about land (Oxen Meadows) and dogs: a farce on greed for property.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: First Flight Prose 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Her father's debts
Oxen Meadows and whose dog is better
The date of the wedding
A lost ring

questions.question: What makes the journey with Mijbil from Iraq to London funny?
questions.explanation: Humour comes from Mijbil's chaos and people's comic guesses; the warmth comes from the bond between man and pet.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: First Flight Prose 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The pilot's jokes
The writer's fear of flying
The chaos in the plane and strangers' wild guesses about what kind of animal he was
Mijbil's long speeches

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true, and R explains why ice 'would suffice' for destruction.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: First Flight Poems 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: In 'Fire and Ice', the poet says that ice would also be enough to destroy the world.
questions.reason: In the poem, ice stands for hatred, which is as destructive as desire (fire).
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Why is the crow and hemlock moment in 'Dust of Snow' striking?
questions.explanation: A small moment in nature, involving usually gloomy symbols, saves part of the poet's day.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: First Flight Poems 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The crow attacks the poet
Things usually seen as gloomy change the poet's bad mood for the better
The hemlock tree is in full bloom
The snow ruins the poet's day completely

questions.question: What is the main contrast in 'A Tiger in the Zoo'?
questions.explanation: The cage–jungle contrast makes the poem a plea against captivity.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: First Flight Poems 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The tiger in a cage versus the tiger free in the jungle
A tiger versus a lion
A young tiger versus an old tiger
Day versus night in the city

questions.question: What does the boy in 'The Ball Poem' learn?
questions.explanation: The poet does not buy him another ball: growing up means accepting loss and responsibility.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: First Flight Poems 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Money can buy back anything he loses
Loss is part of life, and he must learn to bear it himself
Others will always replace what he loses
He should never play with a ball again

questions.question: In Carl Sandburg's 'Fog', the fog is compared to:
questions.explanation: One extended metaphor: the fog comes and goes silently, like a cat.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: First Flight Poems 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: A ship
A tiger
A cloud of smoke
A cat

questions.question: Why is the name 'Amanda' repeated in the poem 'Amanda!'?
questions.explanation: The repeated name sets the tone of constant scolding, from which Amanda escapes into daydreams.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: First Flight Poems 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: To show that Amanda is famous
To show the nagging, scolding tone of the speaker
Because Amanda cannot hear
To introduce a new character

questions.question: What is the message of 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon'?
questions.explanation: The pets who mock Custard flee from the pirate; only Custard fights.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: First Flight Poems 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Pirates are always brave
Do not judge anyone by appearances
Pets should never be kept at home
Cowards are always happy

questions.question: In 'For Anne Gregory', why does the young woman want to dye her hair?
questions.explanation: Inner versus outer beauty: the poet replies that only God could love her 'for herself alone'.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: First Flight Poems 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: She wants to be loved for herself, not for her yellow hair
She is going to a party
She wants to look like the poet
She dislikes the colour yellow

questions.question: How does the vet cure Tricki in 'A Triumph of Surgery'?
questions.explanation: Overfeeding made Tricki ill; diet and exercise cured him. Too much love can harm.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Footprints Without Feet 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: With expensive tonics
With a strict diet and exercise at the vet's surgery
By sending him to another city
With a major operation

questions.question: Why does Hari Singh return the stolen money in 'The Thief's Story'?
questions.explanation: He chooses learning and trust over a life of stealing.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Footprints Without Feet 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: He values the education and trust Anil offers him more than the money
He is caught by the police
He finds the money is fake
Anil threatens him

questions.question: How does Ausable get rid of the armed spy Max in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
questions.explanation: Presence of mind beats force: Max jumps for a balcony that does not exist.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Footprints Without Feet 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: He fights Max and takes his gun
He gives Max a fake report
He calls the police on the phone
He invents a balcony below the window, so Max jumps out

questions.question: What is the irony in 'A Question of Trust'?
questions.explanation: The trickster is tricked; the 'honour among thieves' he expects does not exist.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Footprints Without Feet 1; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The lady returns the jewels
Horace refuses to steal
Horace, a careful thief, is himself tricked by a cleverer thief he trusts
Horace becomes a police officer

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; R is the irony that A refers to. Vanity leads to downfall.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Footprints Without Feet 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: The ending of 'The Necklace' is ironic.
questions.reason: Matilda spends ten years in debt replacing a necklace that turns out to have been fake.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Why does Bholi refuse to marry the groom at the end of 'Bholi'?
questions.explanation: Education gives her the confidence and dignity to reject a dowry-seeking groom.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Footprints Without Feet 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: He is too young
He lives too far away
He is greedy and demands dowry
Her teacher forbids it

questions.question: Why does Think-Tank call off the invasion of Earth in 'The Book that Saved the Earth'?
questions.explanation: His arrogant misreading of nursery rhymes makes him think Earth is dangerous: books win.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Footprints Without Feet 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Earth's army defeats the Martians
The rocket breaks down
Noodle refuses to obey him
He misreads a book of nursery rhymes and panics

questions.question: According to 'The Making of a Scientist', which pair best explains Richard Ebright's success?
questions.explanation: His curiosity about butterflies, his mother's support and science fairs grew into real research.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Footprints Without Feet 2; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Copying other scientists' work
Strict teachers and punishments
Luck and wealth
Curiosity and persistence, encouraged by his mother
